## Standing rules
- Promo links :: Every sleep-Bible video and every promo for any book or channel carries the Kingdom Impact Shop link plus 3-4 relevant book links in the description. Set by Neko Oct 16, 2026.
- Scripture :: KJV only. Do not announce it.
- Derrick :: No 'tomorrow' promises. Never tag people in posts. Nothing posts without Neko's yes on that exact file.
- Money :: Ask before spending any of his money or credits. Prefer free options (Gemini Pro plan).
- Asleep work :: When Neko sleeps: work through the last threads, do the work, put it in overnight/ in the repo. No look-at-this asks.
- Secrets :: Passwords and tokens never in chat.
- Update habit :: After every piece of work, update Status, Next step and Updated on this sheet, commit and push before replying. Updated holds date AND time in Eastern, like 'Oct 16 11:50 PM ET'. Also set Last updated on the Where we are tab to the same stamp.
- One tracker :: This file is the only tracker. Read Tasks, Standing rules and How it was done before answering any where-are-we question or asking Neko for anything. Never create another sheet or tracker. Neko rule Oct 16, 2026.
- Stale check :: Before changing a row, read its Updated stamp. If it is newer than what you last read (another thread worked on it), git pull and reconcile first. Never overwrite a newer row with older information. Always git pull before editing and again before pushing.
- Capacity and archive :: A tab can hold about 1 million rows and the repo file limit is 100 MB, so space is not the limit; readability is. Keep Tasks under about 150 rows. Done rows older than 14 days move to the Archive tab (same columns plus Archived date). Never delete rows.
- Versions :: If the file passes about 300 rows or 1 MB: copy it to overnight/archive/Claude-Work-Tracker-V<n>-<date>.xlsx, then start a clean V<n+1> in the main file with open rows only. V1 baseline is already in overnight/archive/.
- Plain-text mirror :: After every edit run python3 tools/tracker_sync.py. It rebuilds overnight/TRACKER.md, which any thread can read without a spreadsheet library. Commit both files.
- Thread start :: Every thread: read /README.md in the repo root first, then overnight/TRACKER.md. The root README tells you the rules.

## How it was done
- Derrick episode in Flow :: Open Derrick project in Chrome (signed in as neko.husser@gmail.com). Add derrick-gray still as reference, type script clip (about 15 words), generate Veo 3.1 Lite 9:16. Stitch, caption, -14 LUFS in ffmpeg. Send ONE captioned MP4 for approval. :: Project flow.google.com/u/0/project/0a90fb26-707c-45ae-aae4-61a8d163a56b. Keep other Chrome tabs closed. Screenshots in Chrome often time out; use get_page_text.
- Make a new Derrick still in Flow :: Flow side panel: ingredients (+) button, pick derrick-gray.png from the asset list, Add to prompt, type description, send. Agent confirms before generating; image is free (Nano Banana). :: Done Oct 16 for the mic still.
- Animate a still :: Flow shows an Animate button under each still. Check the credit cost shown first; Lite is 10 credits. :: Not tested yet.
- Verse short or sleep video to Buffer :: Render on GitHub Actions, commit mp4 to repo, queue in Buffer (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) with raw.githubusercontent URL. :: Buffer cap 10 queued per channel. See workflow-playbook memory.
- Facebook group post or join :: Built-in browser pane (needs laptop awake, pane visible), logged in as Blessed Prayers. Link posts only. :: About 3 groups a day, read rules first.
- Flow credit saving :: Lite not Quality; one output; 6-7s clips; targeted edits instead of full regenerate; use the free daily 50 credits. :: Source: Google Flow credits help page.
- HeyGen voice fix :: Voice picker, Import from ElevenLabs (Neko types his own API key) or Clone from approved sample. Voice must be ElevenLabs Derrick Hughes, deeper and more masculine. :: Neko does the login/key step.
- Copyright Office (eCO) :: eco.copyright.gov in the built-in browser. Neko does login, payment and audio upload; Claude fills every other field. Suno-made audio is disclosed as AI and excluded from the claim; claim is lyrics and human production (Vaizal transfer of rights). :: Fiverr license letters: fiverr.com/inbox/pesanmusik, open PDF link in the pane and read by screenshot.
- Render a new sleep Bible book :: gh api -X POST repos/<repo>/actions/workflows/sleep-render.yml/dispatches -f ref=main -f inputs[book]=Genesis -f inputs[title]="The Book of Genesis" -f inputs[voice]=af_nicole -f inputs[tag]=sleep-genesis-chapters -f inputs[chunks]=10. Then sleep-master, sleep-qa, sleep-glitch. :: Genesis chapters done Oct 17 (free GitHub minutes, no credits). Book name = file name from aruljohn/Bible-kjv.
- Upload a long sleep video to YouTube :: Psalms way: file downloaded to laptop (curl in device shell into Downloads), then Studio Create > Upload videos > Select files, Neko picks file in the native picker, Claude fills metadata. Or the youtube-upload workflow once the 3 YT secrets exist. :: Did NOT work: fetching GitHub release files from the Studio page (its CSP blocks them); injecting a File into the upload input with a script (blocked by the session safety check); computer-use cannot drive the Claude app window.
- Book chapters via DeepSeek :: Give it the full brief once, then a correction brief: what changed and why, the ban list, a self-check, and the corrected chapter as the standard. DeepSeek writes ahead and invents backstory, so audit every chapter against the brief (names, facts, Scripture quotes, banned phrases) before Neko reads it. Ban list built from tropes.fyi, pangram.com/signs-of-ai-writing, plusai.com overused words, and the humzakt ai-writing-markers dataset; added the sit-with/hold-space family and no em dashes. :: Neko pastes briefs into DeepSeek; Claude audits and fixes. Chapters live in chat only, never as files.
- Glitch-scan a rendered sleep book :: Dispatch the sleep-glitch workflow: gh api -X POST repos/<repo>/actions/workflows/sleep-glitch.yml/dispatches -f ref=main -f inputs[book]=John -f inputs[tag]=sleep-john -f inputs[chunks]=10. About 17 min on free GitHub minutes. It aligns each verse to its audio by duration and writes glitch-NN.json to the release (speed, longest pause, click ratio, word match per verse). Read with tools/rel.sh down <tag> <dir> glitch-. :: John and Proverbs scanned Oct 17: speed uniform, only 4 verses with a pause just over 2 s (John 3:18, 12:38, 21:25, Proverbs 12:11), no clicks, word mismatches are spelling variants or Whisper dropouts. Judged by measurement only; Claude cannot hear audio.
